[Performance introduction]

NANTA, a performance created by Korea and highly praised by the world, since 1997

Nanta is a comical depiction of what happens in the kitchen, based on the rhythm of Samulnori, a traditional Korean melody. 
It is Korea's first non-verbal performance.
Kitchen utensils such as knives and cutting boards are sublimated into wonderful musical instruments, creating a spectacular performance, a surprise traditional wedding, and a performance with the audience. 
With dumpling stacking, traditional Korean dance and samgomu harmonizing with the melody, and drumming with a refreshing ending that will make your heart flutter, etc. 
'Nanta' is a powerful performance that can relieve stress in a fun way for people of all ages and genders, regardless of nationality.

[Performance introduction]

Every Monday in 2026,
Held at Sungkyun Small Theater in Daehakro
Lee Cheol-jin’s story of Seungmu, “Only Seungmu”.


Seungmu (僧舞) is a work of art that represents Korean traditional dance and is a highly aesthetic dance that captures both the spirituality of Buddhist practice and human inner emotions. Jang Sam's delicate lines, controlled breathing and rhythm, and aesthetics of still movement create a world of vitality and deep thought that explodes in silence.

 
This stage is a Seungmu dance presented through an in-depth interpretation by Lee Cheol-jin, a dancer who continues the orthodox lineage that runs from Han Seong-jun, Han Young-sook, and Lee Ae-ju. Having walked a single path as a Buddhist monk for decades, he fully displays the philosophy of dance and the density of time on the stage. In each movement and breath, the accumulated traces of practice and the artist's skills are clearly revealed.

 
〈Only Seungmu〉, which is held as an open run, provides a special time for the audience to face their own inner self through the echo of movement that resonates in silence.

[시놉시스]\n\n01 Living Machines, Mechanical.en:
[Synopsis]

01 Living Machines, Mechanical Life
Living machines, mechanical life: Machines indulge in self-destructive mechanical pleasure through movements that can be repeated infinitely while in operation, and human mortality sometimes causes us to fall into the inhuman power of machines. It suggests the possibility of new life forms through the process where life forms and machines indulge and merge with each other.

02 The Intensity of Fusion
Mechanization of unstoppable impulse: The human brain and nerves have an instinctive impulse to survive, but the mechanical instinct is nothing more than simple repetition. When humans give up their nature and accept mechanical impulses,
It reminds us of the moment when metal and flesh become more deeply intertwined, and makes us imagine the possibility of a new life form being born between humans and non-living things.

03 The Mechanization of Irresistible Impulses
Violence of fusion: The moment when machines and living things collide, lusting after each other, iron and flesh, nerves and metal collide roughly. Sensation and insensibility, life and inanimateness mix together, and the possibility of a new existence arises.
This fusion is not a simple union, but a field of creation where neural explosion and mechanical pressure intersect.
At the moment when metal and skin share lustful friction, the boundary between humans and machines becomes blurred, and a new being called 'pseudo-life' exhales like a herald of birth.

04 The Birth of Artificial Life
Birth of similar life: We are aware of the new life forms or side effects that are born.
Will they live in harmony? Machines with a human scent and humans.
It suggests how we should live in the future.

[Performance introduction]
This performance is a colorful stage that begins with the liveliness of the march and continues with the emotion of the movie music.

Opening the performance, First Suite for Band – Alfred Reed delightfully displays the rhythm and vitality of a wind ensemble with a work consisting of marches, rags, and gallops. The following song, Pearl Harbor, quietly depicts human emotions in the midst of war with its lyrical melody.

In the middle part, John Williams in Concert, which contains the musical world of John Williams, is played, presenting the charm of film music that is both grand and touching. Afterwards, Beauty and the Beast delivers a fairytale-like time to the audience with familiar melodies and a warm atmosphere.

Lastly, Moment for Morricone, a compilation of Ennio Morricone's famous songs, is played, ending the performance with a deep resonance.

[Performance introduction]

Classical guitarist Shin Joo-heon

Classical guitarist Shin Joo-heon, who is praised by both the music industry and the public for his creative ideas and emotional interpretation of works, majored in classical guitar and graduated from the Department of Instrumental Music, College of Music, Seoul National University.

He was recognized for his skills by winning prizes at leading domestic and international guitar competitions, including 1st place at the Korean Music Competition, 1st place at the Overseas Dispatch Competition, 2nd place at the International Music Competition Vienna, 1st place at the France Music Competition Guitar, and 4th place at the Adelaide Guitar Festival. Based on this, he has been invited to perform on major stages such as with orchestras and performances at the Seoul Arts Center, and is continuing his active international activities by giving solo recitals and invited performances in Korea, Tokyo, Japan, and Taichung, Taiwan.

He has collaborated with Seongnam Philharmonic Orchestra, Hanyang University College of Music, and Seoul Haegeum Ensemble, and has been invited as a performer to various festivals and stages to communicate with audiences, including a concert with commentary by Geum Nan-sae, Hyundai Motor Company STAGE

In addition, he served as music director for the IBK Industrial Bank of Korea's Win Class VVIP Concert and as the music general artist for Dokdo LIVE hosted by the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, engaging in activities encompassing planning and performance.

Not limited to classical music, he has also been active in a wide range of popular music and content stages, such as PLAY THE GUITAR, musical performances, Nexon game music concerts, and various album production sessions, establishing himself as a performer who crosses the boundary between classical and popular music.

Recently, he has attempted to harmonize Eastern and Western music by collaborating with a number of Korean traditional music players, including duo activities with haegeum player Noh Eun-ah, and is continuously expanding his musical spectrum.

Meanwhile, his music is widely loved by the general public and music lovers at home and abroad through broadcast appearances such as SBS Amazing Competition Star King, KBS Music Room, and KBS Korean Traditional Music Festival, as well as YouTube and SNS content media.

He is currently teaching at Seoul Arts High School, Gyeonggi Arts High School, and Yewon School, and served as a conductor and music director for guitar ensemble classes at the former Armed Forces Financial Management Corps. In addition, he is striving to nurture younger students by running Shin Joo-heon's guitar class, and was awarded the Korea Guitar Association's Outstanding Leader Award.

In addition, he received the Korea Best Brand Cultural Artist Award in recognition of his musical achievements and contribution to the field of culture and arts.

Continuing his various activities, he is currently attracting attention as a next-generation guitar player, captivating the hearts of audiences with his beautiful tone and technically sophisticated performance.

[Performance introduction]
This performance is an interpretive performance that combines Arirang, sanjo, folk songs, and popular melodies with the traditional gayageum and 25-string gayageum. It introduces the depth of traditional music and modern reinterpretation, and proposes an intimate musical experience that communicates with the audience in a salon space.

[PROGRAM]
* Two Arari 
This is a performance piece that newly arranged Jeongseon, Gangwon-do, Haeju, and Jindo Arirang into traditional gayageum and 25-string gayageum. It is a lyrical opening song that conveys the emotion of Korean folk songs through various gayageum tones.

* Kimjukparyu Gayageum Sanjo 
Kim Juk-pa is a master who established the flow of gayageum sanjo in the 20th century. Kimjukparyu Sanjo is a representative piece that shows the artistry and skills of the performer with its delicate Sigimsae, various playing techniques, and gradually faster beats.

* <A Million Roses> 
A Million Roses is widely known as Shim Soo-bong's song in Korea, but it began with the song <The Life of a Girl Given by Marinya>, which was released in Latvia in 1981. It contains a mythological story about the goddess of the earth and fate, Mara, suffering because she forgot to give happiness to her daughter. It was later rewritten into Russian and became widely known as a love song, and today's performance tells the story of how this melody traveled across borders.

* 25-string gayageum <Doraji Taryeong>
This is a performance piece that reinterprets the representative folk song of the Gangwon-Gyeonggi region, <Bolaji Taryeong>, using the wide vocal range and harmony of the 25-string gayageum.

* Memories engraved in my heart - <Cheommilmil> 
The theme song ‘Wolryang Representative Ah Jeoksim’ and ‘I’m Still Loving You’ from the movie <Cheommilmil> are played on two gayageums.

Daleum’s second regular album, “Coexistence,” is a musical work that depicts the harmony and balance created by different beings under the theme of ‘living together.’
This performance is centered around the sound of coexistence created by two traditional string instruments, the gayageum and geomungo. The program begins with ‘Dasreum’ based on traditional modes and continues through ‘Tal’, ‘dot’, ‘The Waves’, ‘Cracking’, and ‘Alive’, showing a musical narrative where tradition and modernity intersect. Each song expresses everyday emotions, cracks, recovery, and the energy of life in various ways and is structured so that the audience can comfortably immerse themselves in it. Daleum's unique performance style, which maintains the depth of traditional music while adding a modern sensibility, will provide a new experience to the audience.

[시놉시스]\n\n2001년 9월 4일 월요일 오전 7시 39분. 한 소.en:
[Synopsis]

Monday, September 4, 2001, 7:39 AM. The moment a girl takes her steps, time becomes undifferentiated and stops. The girl closes her eyes, sneezes, and floats in the air.
In that moment, a perfect rainbow at an angle of 42 degrees unfolds before your eyes. The seven-color panorama from red to purple is replaced with everyday objects such as trains, sheet music, jackets, and swimsuits, filling the stage. The seven notes of Doremi Fasolassido overlap to create a huge chord, but the girl who is the protagonist of that moment is unaware of this wonderful cosmic phenomenon.
Starting from a sneeze, time flows back and forth. People around me, friendship, dating, learning. The girl looks at the world by breaking it into small pieces, and reaches sadness and resentment within it.
So the girl sneezes, breathing and spitting out all of this with all her might.

Since then, the three-year threshold has moved forward with a new breath, and Lane stands at the beginning again.

Lane redefines the meaning of the team name from 'Rain', which symbolizes comfort, to 'Rain (來潾)', which symbolizes coming clarity.

Dreaming of a place where clear sound always flows (來潾) and the sound of people visiting (來人) never ceases (來人), this performance shares the excitement and anticipation of the beginning, a little fear, and yet a cheerful heartbeat through music.

Following Kim Dan-bi's in-depth commentary and witty and witty progress, the performance and story naturally continue, and the audience crosses the time of a new beginning while listening to the music.
